# First-cell keepNext controls

Original manually authored OOXML, generated by `tools/first_cell_keep_fixture.py`.
The base package skeleton comes from this repository's original cell-end-context
fixture. No third-party template or document-engine implementation is included.
Native PDFs were exported by the reference application with
`tools/export-reference.ps1`. `tools/record_first_cell_keep.py` records source
and PDF hashes and marker page assignments independently of the app.

Thirteen controls contain 27 native pages. A tall preceding paragraph leaves room
for part of a table row. The six-line cell would ordinarily split across pages.

- none/middle/right: normal row split.
- left: first cell's first paragraph has keepNext; the reference application moves the whole row.
- first-only/all-left: later paragraphs in that cell do not remove this row keep.
- last-only/empty-first-off: a later paragraph's flag does not add a row keep.
- empty-left: the first paragraph may be empty and still add the row keep.
- merge-first: a first cell spanning two grid columns retains the behavior.
- oversized: the row starts on the next page, then splits when larger than a page.
- two-rows/two-rows-off: a short first row does not require the entire following
  row to fit; both variants have the same page boundaries. The separate
  row-keep-fitting controls establish reservation of the following row's start.

ECMA-376 Part 1 section 17.3.1.15 defines paragraph keepNext and chained keeps,
without this special first-cell row-splitting interpretation. The controls prove
the reference application's additional row-level behavior while preserving ordinary per-cell keeps.
This does not establish all combinations with vertical merges, omitted leading
grid cells, nested tables or compatibility modes; existing regression suites cover
related pagination paths and further native edge cases remain in scope.
